content.title: Amy Madigan Is Your Best-Supporting-Actress Winner at Oscars 2026
content.text: Throw on that red wig and smear that lipstick, because Aunt Gladys is here to stay. Stalwart actor Amy Madigan just took home the 2026 Oscar for best supporting actress for her role as Aunt Gladys, the creepy caretaker who steals the third act of Zach Cregger’s horror-comedy Weapons.“This is great!” she said from the stage, after letting loose a very Aunt Gladys-esque laugh. Madigan also thanked Cregger. “As you can tell, I’m really flummoxed,” she added, before paying tribute to her fellow nominees by name. “When I was doing all the Weapons stuff, I was kinda traveling on my own, and people from One Battle and people from Sinners just kind of gave me a hug and said come on in.”Madigan faced stiff competition from her fellow nominees: Teyana Taylor for One Battle After Another; Wunmi Mosaku for Sinners; and costars Elle Fanning and Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas for Sentimental Value. Three of the five have been trading awards back and forth all season long.After winning at the Critics Choice Awards—and delivering a sincere and crowd-pleasing speech—Madigan lost the Golden Globe to Taylor. Prognosticating got even more complicated when Mosaku took home the BAFTA. Between Mosaku, Madigan, and Taylor, it was anyone’s guess who would win best supporting actress this year. But at the Actor Awards, it became clear who ultimately had the edge: Madigan. With that major precursor under her belt, Madigan proved she could score with the Academy’s largest voting branch and—despite the front-runner status of One Battle After Another and Sinners’ late-breaking surge—she was poised to repeat at the Oscars. And repeat she has.It’s been a long time since Madigan was recognized by the Academy Awards. She was first nominated 40 years ago in this same category for her work in 1985’s Twice in a Lifetime. Since then, Madigan has been a go-to character actor onstage and onscreen. Her kooky yet malevolent Aunt Gladys instantly struck a nerve with audiences, inspiring plenty of memes and Halloween costumes.Madigan ended her speech by thanking her husband of 40 years, four-time Oscar nominee Ed Harris.See What the Oscars 2026 Nominees Wore to Their First Academy Awards1 / 13Steve Granitz/WireImageTimothée Chalamet, 2018In Berluti.
